title: Freed from embryonic signals, frog skin cells form self-motile Xenobots

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Freed from embryonic signals, frog skin cells form self-motile Xenobots

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Frog (Xenopus) embryonic epithelial cells, which in vivo form a passive protective outer layer, instead form Xenobots (functional, self-motile constructs with novel behaviours) when liberated from the instructive influences of other cells, showing that such behaviours are normally suppressed by signalling from neighbouring cells during development.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2023, Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology › Scaling up from cellular competency to collective intelligence

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: However, when liberated from the instructive influences of the other cells, frog epithelial cells instead form a Xenobot—a functional, self-motile construct with many novel behaviors that are normally suppressed and hidden by the instructive signaling of other cells during development [125].

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology”, Cellular and molecular life sciences : CMLS (2023), doi:10.1007/s00018-023-04790-z; section “Scaling up from cellular competency to collective intelligence”. Scope: Xenopus laevis embryonic ectoderm explants

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2023-agential-05: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.69

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Formation and motility are directly quantifiable and reported in a defined preparation. Publicly available published records can test the phenomenon, but cleanly assigning suppression to instructive neighbour signals requires controls or data that may not be deposited.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare isolated Xenopus ectoderm explants with intact or signal-restored controls for spheroid formation, ciliary motility, trajectories, and behaviours. The suppression inference requires showing that reintroducing specific neighbouring-cell signals blocks behaviours without nonspecific toxicity.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Published demonstrations may not expose raw videos and trajectories.

Novel behaviour does not alone show active in-vivo suppression.

Isolation changes mechanics and medium as well as signalling.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:

data existence: 0.62
analysis feasibility: 0.78
data adequacy: 0.58
operationalizability: 0.88

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The explant contrast is concrete and the design pipeline's code is public, but the biological outcome is documented as published experimental reports from the same research program rather than a reusable tracking dataset. Those reports can be checked for whether motile aggregates were produced. They do not isolate the neighbour signals supposed to suppress the behaviour, so the suppression clause stays partly untested.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare motility and collective behaviour of Xenopus embryonic epidermal cells dissociated from the embryo with intact embryonic epidermis. Self-motile aggregates formed from those cells, and absent while the cells remain in place, would support the explant result; failure to form motile constructs under the published dissociation protocol would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Ciliary motility used for mucus clearance in vivo can look like a novel behaviour once cells are free in culture.

Trial-level videos and counts sit in the original papers' supplements, not in an independent data repository.
